sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is on the main floor of the McMinn courthouse, 6 East Madison Avenue, Athens, TN 37303, phone (423) 745-1232. The counter is open from half past eight in the morning until four in the afternoon.

Staff record conveyances, deeds of trust, leases and similar instruments, and they certify copies of anything on file. Voters choose the register countywide every four years. A seller here does not usually visit in person, because the deed that transfers your house to a buyer normally comes from the closing agent.

The county's register page says the counter takes debit and credit cards, American Express excluded. Ask the staff for a total when your deed runs long.

Athens is the county seat and the biggest city, and Etowah, Niota and Sweetwater are cities too. The county had 57,404 residents in July 2025, a 7.8% gain over April 2020, and 24,424 housing units. Owners occupy 75.8% of homes, the typical owner-occupied value is $211,800, rent in the middle is $803, and household income in the middle is $61,470. Builders took out 125 permits in 2025.

Three school systems serve the county. McMinn County Schools operates both high schools, with Athens City Schools and the Etowah School District teaching grades K through 8 inside their boundaries.

Two state taxes apply at recording. The transfer tax is 37 cents for each $100 of the sale price or property value, whichever is higher. The mortgage tax is 11.5 cents for each $100 borrowed, and the first $2,000 of any debt is left out. The register collects both on the spot, and the grantee shown on the deed carries the transfer tax.

Tennessee recordation taxes collected at the McMinn County register

A purchase contract can reassign these costs, so read yours before closing. Your closing agent will total the taxes for your deal.

sections.h2: What the register requires before recording
sections.html:
McMinn County posts a checklist called Requirements to Record Documents. A deed missing one of its items risks rejection, so go through it with whoever prepares your closing papers.

  • Preparer's name and address, matching the return envelope if you enclose one.
  • Grantee's address, along with the address for future tax bills.
  • Map and parcel number, legal description, and last book and page of title.
  • Each signature notarized, with the acknowledgment naming the signers and carrying the notary's seal and date.
  • A sworn oath of consideration giving whichever is larger, the price or the property's value.
  • For any document tied to debt, the sentence "Maximum principal indebtedness for TN tax recording purposes is $___."

A corrected document needs fresh signatures and acknowledgments, or a scrivener's affidavit stapled to it. Documents sent without a stamped, self-addressed return envelope may be destroyed 90 days after recording, so include one if you want the original back.

sections.h2: Transfers with no realty transfer tax
sections.html:
Some transfers escape the $0.37 tax under the state manual, and a few matter in family and estate sales. Exempt transfers need no oath.

  • Transfers of a leasehold estate.
  • One spouse deeding to the other as a tenancy by the entirety begins or ends.
  • A deed signed by an executor to carry out a gift in a will.
  • Domestic decrees and deeds that adjust property rights between divorcing spouses.
  • Moves into or back out of a revocable living trust made by that owner or the owner's spouse.
  • Conveyances to or from a government body.

A quitclaim deed is taxed on the consideration given, yet the state taxes fair market value when its wording shows an intent to pass the property itself, such as "in fee simple." State revenue staff sometimes pull deeds from a random county and date range, set the sworn value beside the assessor's figure, and mail an inquiry letter if the two are far apart. An unusually low stated price on a McMinn County deed can draw that letter.

The register accepts electronic recordings through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company (CSC) and eRecording Partners Network (EPN). Your title company will pick one of these routes at closing.

For searching, the county points researchers to US Title Search Network, which charges per search or a monthly fee. If that service gives you trouble, the register's page lists Progress Inc. at 1 (800) 394-7477. Assessor data is separate: the Assessor of Property, at (423) 745-2743, keeps parcel maps and property cards, and the state's assessment website lets you look up the map and parcel numbers that every conveyance needs.

If you inherited a McMinn County house and need to sell, ask the register how the executor's deed should be worded, and ask the probate clerk for proof of authority.

sections.h2: Property tax when a McMinn County house sells
sections.html:
County property tax goes to the McMinn County Trustee in the courthouse at 6 East Madison Avenue, phone (423) 745-1291. The current year's bill can be paid between October 1 and the end of February. Weekday hours are 8 to 4, and the office also opens on Saturday mornings in February.

The Trustee also handles applications for the state's Tax Relief Program, which helps elderly and disabled homeowners and disabled-veteran owners. The application cutoff is 35 days after the February 28 payment deadline. Relief repays part of a bill the owner has paid, so the bill itself still arrives.

Settlement of the current year's tax is a closing-table decision, so raise it with the closing agent early and get a payoff from the Trustee beforehand. If the owner name or mailing address on the roll is wrong, the assessor can fix it. Once the deed is recorded here, the sale is on the public record, and the title company can confirm that no earlier lien is still open.

faqs.q: Where is a McMinn County deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the McMinn County Register of Deeds, in the Athens courthouse at 6 East Madison Avenue. Call (423) 745-1232 with questions. Title companies normally submit deeds electronically.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax applies when a McMinn County house sells?
faqs.a: Thirty-seven cents per $100 of the larger of price or value. The grantee owes it unless the contract shifts it.

faqs.q: Can a deed be e-recorded in McMinn County?
faqs.a: Yes. The register takes e-recordings from Simplifile, CSC and eRecording Partners Network. Individuals without an account usually rely on a title company or attorney.

faqs.q: Is transfer tax owed on a sale of an inherited McMinn County house?
faqs.a: A deed an executor signs to carry out a gift in a will is exempt. The later sale to a buyer is taxed at the normal rate, so ask the register how each deed in the chain is treated.

faqs.q: Where is McMinn County property tax paid ahead of a closing?
faqs.a: Pay the McMinn County Trustee at the courthouse in Athens and call (423) 745-1291 for a payoff figure. Current-year bills are payable October 1 through the end of February.
